metadata.author: Greg Paskal
metadata.description: DNS security and configuration issues finding template with comprehensive guidance for all audiences including missing DNSSEC, CAA records, SPF/DKIM/DMARC email authentication, DNS hijacking vulnerabilities, and DNS hardening procedures across authoritative nameservers and DNS providers.

EXECUTIVE.summary: Your DNS infrastructure lacks critical security protections including DNSSEC, CAA records, and email authentication (SPF/DKIM/DMARC), exposing your organization to DNS hijacking, fraudulent SSL certificates, email spoofing, and phishing attacks using your domain.
EXECUTIVE.businessRisk: Critical risk of brand impersonation and domain hijacking. Without DNS security: Attackers can issue fraudulent SSL certificates for your domain (if CAA missing), hijack email domains for phishing campaigns (if SPF/DKIM/DMARC missing), redirect users to malicious sites via DNS poisoning (if DNSSEC missing), launch phishing attacks using your domain name, damage brand reputation through email spoofing. Email providers (Gmail, Microsoft) increasingly require DMARC for delivery - missing DMARC causes legitimate emails to be rejected or marked as spam. Google/Yahoo mandate DMARC for bulk senders (Feb 2024). Average phishing attack costs $4.91M (IBM 2023). Brand damage from spoofed emails is immeasurable. Lost customer trust and revenue.
EXECUTIVE.complianceImpact: DMARC enforcement mandate (Google/Yahoo Feb 2024) - emails may be rejected without DMARC. NIST 800-81-2 recommends DNSSEC deployment. CIS DNS Benchmark requires DNS security controls. Email authentication gaps flagged in security audits. Industry best practices require SPF/DKIM/DMARC. Regulatory requirements for email security (HIPAA, GDPR data integrity). Customer security questionnaires fail without DNS security.

PROJECT_MANAGER.summary: DNS infrastructure missing security controls: DNSSEC for DNS integrity, CAA records to restrict certificate issuance, SPF/DKIM/DMARC for email authentication. Need DNS security implementation to prevent hijacking and email spoofing.
PROJECT_MANAGER.timeline: Should be addressed within 1-2 sprints. Implementation takes 3-6 hours depending on DNS provider. High priority if sending bulk email or preparing for compliance audit. Critical if recent phishing attempts using your domain reported. Email authentication (SPF/DKIM/DMARC) is highest priority due to 2024 enforcement mandates.
PROJECT_MANAGER.effort: 3-6 hours for complete DNS security implementation. SPF/DKIM/DMARC: 2-3 hours (highest priority). CAA records: 1 hour. DNSSEC: 2-3 hours (complex, provider-dependent). Testing and monitoring: 1-2 hours. One-time implementation with periodic review (quarterly).
dependencies: Access to DNS management console (Route53, Cloudflare, etc.)
List of authorized email senders (for SPF)
List of authorized certificate authorities (for CAA)
Email team for DMARC policy coordination

DEVELOPER.summary: DNS records lack security controls: DNSSEC signatures for authenticity, CAA records restricting certificate issuance, SPF records authorizing mail servers, DKIM signatures for email integrity, DMARC policies for handling failures.
DEVELOPER.technical: DNS security gaps: 1) DNSSEC - cryptographic signatures prevent DNS poisoning and cache poisoning attacks. Uses DS records at parent zone, DNSKEY records at zone, RRSIG records signing resource records. 2) CAA (Certificate Authority Authorization) - DNS record specifying which CAs can issue certificates for domain. Format: 'CAA 0 issue "letsencrypt.org"'. Prevents fraudulent certificate issuance. 3) SPF (Sender Policy Framework) - TXT record listing authorized mail servers. Format: 'v=spf1 include:_spf.google.com ~all'. 4) DKIM (DomainKeys Identified Mail) - cryptographic signature in email headers, validated via DNS TXT record containing public key. 5) DMARC (Domain-based Message Authentication) - policy for handling SPF/DKIM failures. Format: 'v=DMARC1; p=reject; rua=mailto:dmarc@domain.com'. Without these: DNS responses can be spoofed, fraudulent certificates issued, emails forged, phishing attacks using domain name.
DEVELOPER.vulnerability: CWE-350 (Reliance on Reverse DNS Resolution) - DNS responses trusted without validation. CWE-923 (Improper Restriction of Communication Channel to Intended Endpoints) - No authentication of DNS responses. CVE-2008-1447 (Kaminsky DNS cache poisoning) - DNSSEC prevents. Email spoofing enables: phishing campaigns using your domain, CEO fraud attacks, credential harvesting, malware distribution, brand impersonation. DNS hijacking enables: traffic redirection to malicious sites, man-in-the-middle attacks, credential theft via fake login pages. Missing CAA allows: any CA to issue certificates for your domain, fraudulent certificates enabling MITM attacks.

SECURITY_ENGINEER.summary: DNS infrastructure lacks multiple security layers: DNSSEC (integrity), CAA (certificate control), SPF/DKIM/DMARC (email authentication), creating high-severity vulnerability to DNS hijacking, email spoofing, and man-in-the-middle attacks.
SECURITY_ENGINEER.vulnerability: CWE-350 (Reliance on Reverse DNS), CWE-923 (Improper Channel Restriction), CVE-2008-1447 (DNS cache poisoning). Multiple DNS security gaps create layered vulnerabilities: Missing DNSSEC enables DNS poisoning/hijacking, missing CAA enables fraudulent certificate issuance, missing SPF/DKIM/DMARC enables email spoofing and phishing. These vulnerabilities compound: DNS hijacking + fraudulent certificate = complete MITM capability. Email spoofing + brand trust = highly effective phishing.
SECURITY_ENGINEER.attackVector: 1) DNS Cache Poisoning: Attacker poisons recursive resolver cache with malicious DNS records, redirecting users to attacker-controlled servers. 2) DNS Hijacking: Compromise DNS provider credentials or exploit DNS server, modify records to redirect traffic. 3) Email Spoofing: Forge email headers using victim's domain, bypass spam filters (no SPF/DKIM/DMARC), launch phishing campaigns, CEO fraud, credential harvesting. 4) Fraudulent Certificate Issuance: Request certificate from any CA (no CAA restriction), obtain valid certificate for victim domain, use for MITM attacks or phishing sites. 5) Subdomain Takeover: Find orphaned DNS records pointing to unclaimed resources (S3, GitHub Pages), claim resource, serve malicious content on victim's subdomain. 6) Combined Attack: Hijack DNS + issue fraudulent cert + host phishing site = complete domain impersonation.
SECURITY_ENGINEER.threatLevel: HIGH - DNS attacks are prevalent and high-impact. DNS hijacking incidents: GoDaddy (2020), Amazon Route53 (2019), numerous registrar compromises. Email spoofing universal - 3.4 billion spoofed emails daily (Proofpoint 2023). Missing DMARC results in 60% of spoofed emails delivered to inbox. Missing CAA documented in certificate mis-issuance incidents. DNSSEC adoption still low (30% of domains) making non-DNSSEC domains attractive targets. Low technical skill required for email spoofing (easy to forge headers). DNS hijacking requires higher skill but available via exploit kits and compromised registrar accounts.
SECURITY_ENGINEER.mitigationUrgency: HIGH PRIORITY - Implement within 1-2 weeks. Email authentication (SPF/DKIM/DMARC) is CRITICAL - implement immediately due to Gmail/Yahoo enforcement (Feb 2024). Missing DMARC causes email delivery failures. CAA records take 15 minutes to add - do immediately. DNSSEC implementation more complex (2-3 hours) but essential for DNS integrity. If email spoofing incidents reported: escalate to CRITICAL, implement DMARC p=reject immediately. If DNS hijacking suspected: escalate to CRITICAL, implement DNSSEC and audit DNS provider security.

OPS_INFRASTRUCTURE.summary: Authoritative nameservers lack DNSSEC signing, CAA records, and email authentication records (SPF/DKIM/DMARC), requiring DNS configuration updates across all domains and delegation to DNS provider.
OPS_INFRASTRUCTURE.technical: DNS security implementation: 1) SPF - Add TXT record: 'v=spf1 include:_spf.domain.com include:amazonses.com ~all'. List all authorized mail servers. Use 'include:' for third parties. Use '~all' (soft fail) initially, then '-all' (hard fail). 2) DKIM - Generate key pair (2048-bit RSA), publish public key in DNS TXT record at selector._domainkey.domain.com, configure mail server to sign with private key. 3) DMARC - Add TXT record at _dmarc.domain.com: 'v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:dmarc@domain.com'. Start with p=none (monitor), progress to p=quarantine, then p=reject. 4) CAA - Add CAA record: 'example.com CAA 0 issue "letsencrypt.org"'. List all authorized CAs. Use 'issuewild' for wildcard restrictions. 5) DNSSEC - Enable at DNS provider (Route53, Cloudflare), add DS record at parent nameserver (registrar), configure DNSSEC signing for zone. Provider-dependent process. Implementation points: DNS provider console (Route53, Cloudflare, Google DNS), registrar (for DS record), mail server (DKIM signing), monitoring (DMARC reports).
OPS_INFRASTRUCTURE.scope: All domains and subdomains under organization control: primary domain, subdomains, alternate domains, development/staging domains (if public-facing). Email-sending domains require SPF/DKIM/DMARC. All HTTPS domains should have CAA. All critical domains should have DNSSEC. Coordinate with: DNS provider/hosting, email service provider (Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, SendGrid, SES), SSL/TLS certificate provider, registrar (for DNSSEC DS records). Changes propagate via DNS (TTL), typically 5 minutes to 48 hours.
OPS_INFRASTRUCTURE.monitoring: Monitor DNS security posture: DNSSEC validation (dnssec-analyzer.verisignlabs.com), CAA record checks (caatest.co.uk), SPF validation (mxtoolbox.com/spf.aspx), DKIM validation (mail-tester.com), DMARC reports (aggregate and forensic). Receive DMARC reports daily (rua=mailto:dmarc@domain.com), analyze for: authentication pass/fail rates, sources of legitimate/illegitimate email, spoofing attempts. Set up monitoring: DMARC report analyzer (Postmark, Dmarcian, DMARC Analyzer), DNS monitoring (changes, outages), certificate transparency logs (for unauthorized certificate issuance). Alert on: DNSSEC validation failures, SPF/DKIM failures above threshold, DMARC policy violations, unauthorized certificate issuance (if CAA violated).

QA_TESTER.summary: DNS security gaps prevent validation that domain is protected against hijacking and spoofing. Cannot verify DNSSEC integrity, CAA certificate restrictions, or email authentication without proper DNS records.
QA_TESTER.testImplication: Cannot validate DNS security controls. Security scanning tools flag missing DNSSEC, CAA, SPF, DKIM, DMARC as HIGH severity. Cannot test email deliverability without DMARC (emails rejected by Gmail/Yahoo). Cannot verify certificate issuance controls without CAA. Cannot test DNS integrity without DNSSEC. After implementation, must test: DNSSEC validation passes, CAA prevents unauthorized certificate requests, SPF/DKIM/DMARC authentication succeeds, email deliverability maintained.
QA_TESTER.riskIfNotFixed: Security assessment failure. Penetration testing findings (DNS security gaps). Email deliverability failure (Gmail/Yahoo reject emails without DMARC). Customer security questionnaire failures. Actual exploitation: DNS hijacked redirecting users to malicious sites, fraudulent SSL certificates issued enabling phishing sites, email spoofed for phishing campaigns targeting customers/employees, brand reputation damage from successful impersonation attacks. Bug bounty payouts for subdomain takeover.

generic.code:
# Generic DNS Security Implementation Guide

## 1. SPF (Sender Policy Framework)

### Create SPF Record:
Type: TXT
Name: @ (or your domain)
Value: v=spf1 [mechanisms] [qualifier]

### Common Mechanisms:
- ip4:192.0.2.0/24 - Allow specific IP
- include:_spf.google.com - Include another domain's SPF
- a - Allow domain's A record
- mx - Allow domain's MX records

### Qualifiers:
- + Pass (default)
- ~ Soft fail (mark but don't reject)
- - Hard fail (reject)
- ? Neutral

### Example SPF Records:
# Google Workspace only:
v=spf1 include:_spf.google.com ~all

# Google + AWS SES:
v=spf1 include:_spf.google.com include:amazonses.com ~all

# Multiple providers:
v=spf1 include:_spf.google.com include:sendgrid.net include:_spf.salesforce.com ~all

### SPF Best Practices:
- Start with ~all (soft fail), move to -all after testing
- Limit DNS lookups to 10 (SPF limit)
- Use ip4/ip6 instead of 'a' or 'mx' when possible
- Test with mail-tester.com

## 2. DKIM (DomainKeys Identified Mail)

### Generate DKIM Keys:
# OpenSSL method:
openssl genrsa -out dkim_private.pem 2048
openssl rsa -in dkim_private.pem -pubout -outform der 2>/dev/null | openssl base64 -A

### Create DKIM DNS Record:
Type: TXT
Name: selector._domainkey.yourdomain.com
Value: v=DKIM1; k=rsa; p=MIGfMA0GCSqGSIb3DQEBAQUAA...

### Common Selectors:
- default._domainkey
- google._domainkey (Google Workspace)
- s1._domainkey, s2._domainkey (rotation)

### DKIM Configuration:
1. Generate key pair (2048-bit minimum)
2. Add public key to DNS
3. Configure mail server with private key
4. Test with mail-tester.com

## 3. DMARC (Domain-based Message Authentication)

### Create DMARC Record:
Type: TXT
Name: _dmarc.yourdomain.com
Value: v=DMARC1; p=policy; rua=mailto:reports@yourdomain.com

### DMARC Policies:
- p=none - Monitor only (start here)
- p=quarantine - Suspicious email to spam
- p=reject - Reject failed email

### DMARC Tags:
- v=DMARC1 - Version (required)
- p=policy - Policy for domain (required)
- sp=policy - Policy for subdomains
- rua=mailto: - Aggregate reports
- ruf=mailto: - Forensic reports
- pct=100 - Percentage of email to apply policy
- fo=1 - Forensic report options
- adkim=s - DKIM alignment (s=strict, r=relaxed)
- aspf=s - SPF alignment

### Example DMARC Records:
# Phase 1: Monitor
v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:dmarc@yourdomain.com

# Phase 2: Quarantine
v=DMARC1; p=quarantine; rua=mailto:dmarc@yourdomain.com; pct=50

# Phase 3: Reject
v=DMARC1; p=reject; rua=mailto:dmarc@yourdomain.com; ruf=mailto:dmarc-forensic@yourdomain.com; fo=1

### DMARC Implementation Phases:
1. Week 1: p=none, monitor reports
2. Week 2-3: Analyze, fix SPF/DKIM issues
3. Week 4: p=quarantine; pct=10
4. Week 5-6: p=quarantine; pct=50
5. Week 7: p=quarantine; pct=100
6. Week 8+: p=reject

## 4. CAA (Certificate Authority Authorization)

### Create CAA Record:
Type: CAA
Name: @ (or your domain)
Value: flags tag "value"

### CAA Tags:
- issue - Authorize CA for certificates
- issuewild - Authorize CA for wildcard certificates
- iodef - Report policy violations

### Example CAA Records:
# Let's Encrypt only:
0 issue "letsencrypt.org"
0 issuewild "letsencrypt.org"

# Multiple CAs:
0 issue "letsencrypt.org"
0 issue "digicert.com"
0 issuewild "letsencrypt.org"
0 iodef "mailto:security@yourdomain.com"

# Prevent all issuance:
0 issue ";"

## 5. DNSSEC

### DNSSEC Implementation:
1. Enable DNSSEC at DNS provider
2. Provider generates KSK and ZSK
3. Provider signs zone with RRSIG records
4. Get DS record from provider
5. Add DS record at registrar
6. Wait for propagation (24-48 hours)
7. Verify with dnssec-analyzer.verisignlabs.com

### DNSSEC Components:
- DNSKEY - Public keys
- RRSIG - Signatures
- DS - Delegation Signer (at parent)
- NSEC/NSEC3 - Authenticated denial

### Provider-Specific DNSSEC:
- Route53: Automated, enable in console
- Cloudflare: Automated, one-click enable
- Google Cloud DNS: Automated
- Manual: Use 'dnssec-keygen' and 'dnssec-signzone'
generic.testCode:
# DNS Security Testing Commands

## SPF Testing:
# Check SPF record
dig +short TXT example.com | grep spf
nslookup -type=TXT example.com

# Validate SPF
curl "https://mxtoolbox.com/api/v1/lookup/spf/example.com"

## DKIM Testing:
# Check DKIM record (replace 'selector')
dig +short TXT selector._domainkey.example.com

# Send test email and verify DKIM signature
# Use mail-tester.com or dmarcian.com

## DMARC Testing:
# Check DMARC record
dig +short TXT _dmarc.example.com
nslookup -type=TXT _dmarc.example.com

# Validate DMARC
curl "https://mxtoolbox.com/api/v1/lookup/dmarc/example.com"

## CAA Testing:
# Check CAA records
dig +short CAA example.com
nslookup -type=CAA example.com

# Test with online tool
curl "https://caatest.co.uk/example.com"

## DNSSEC Testing:
# Check DNSSEC
dig +dnssec example.com

# Validate DNSSEC chain
delv example.com

# Online DNSSEC validation
curl "https://dnssec-analyzer.verisignlabs.com/example.com"

## Comprehensive DNS Test:
# Check all records at once
dig example.com ANY

# Use online tools:
# - https://mxtoolbox.com/SuperTool.aspx
# - https://dnschecker.org/
# - https://intodns.com/

## Send Test Email:
# Send to: check-auth@verifier.port25.com
# Or: test@mail-tester.com
# Check DKIM, SPF, DMARC results
generic.dependencies: dig, nslookup, curl, optional: delv for DNSSEC

verificationSteps: 1. Check SPF: dig +short TXT example.com | grep spf
2. Verify SPF includes all authorized mail servers
3. Check DMARC: dig +short TXT _dmarc.example.com
4. Verify DMARC policy is at least p=quarantine (eventually p=reject)
5. Check DKIM: dig +short TXT selector._domainkey.example.com
6. Verify DKIM public key present
7. Send test email to check-auth@verifier.port25.com
8. Verify SPF, DKIM, DMARC all PASS

10. Verify CAA authorizes only intended CAs
11. Check DNSSEC: dig +dnssec example.com
12. Verify DNSSEC validated (AD flag set)
13. Run comprehensive test: https://mxtoolbox.com/SuperTool.aspx
14. Monitor DMARC reports for authentication failures

dns-provider.config:
# DNS Provider Configuration
# Applicable to: Route53, Cloudflare, Google Cloud DNS, etc.

## 1. SPF Record Implementation
Type: TXT
Name: @ (or example.com)
TTL: 300 (5 minutes)
Value: "v=spf1 include:_spf.google.com include:amazonses.com ~all"

Notes:
- List ALL services that send email on your behalf
- Use 'include:' for third-party services
- Start with '~all' (soft fail), progress to '-all' (hard fail)
- Keep under 10 DNS lookups (SPF limit)

## 2. DKIM Record Implementation
Type: TXT
Name: selector._domainkey.example.com
TTL: 300
Value: "v=DKIM1; k=rsa; p=MIGfMA0GCSqGSI..."

Notes:
- Get DKIM values from your email provider
- Google Workspace: google._domainkey
- AWS SES: Generate in SES console
- Multiple selectors for key rotation

## 3. DMARC Record Implementation
Type: TXT
Name: _dmarc.example.com
TTL: 300
Value: "v=DMARC1; p=quarantine; rua=mailto:dmarc-reports@example.com; ruf=mailto:dmarc-forensic@example.com; fo=1; pct=100"

Notes:
- Phase 1: p=none (monitor)
- Phase 2: p=quarantine (suspicious to spam)
- Phase 3: p=reject (block failed)
- Set up email addresses for reports (rua, ruf)
- Monitor reports weekly, adjust policy

## 4. CAA Record Implementation
Type: CAA
Name: @ (or example.com)
TTL: 300
Value: 
  0 issue "letsencrypt.org"
  0 issue "digicert.com"
  0 issuewild "letsencrypt.org"
  0 iodef "mailto:security@example.com"

Notes:
- List ONLY authorized Certificate Authorities
- Use 'issuewild' to restrict wildcard certificates
- Use 'iodef' to receive violation reports
- Add CAA for root domain and subdomains if needed

## 5. DNSSEC Implementation
Provider-Specific:

### AWS Route53:
1. Console → Route53 → Hosted zones
2. Select zone → DNSSEC signing
3. Enable DNSSEC signing
4. Copy DS record (Key tag, Algorithm, Digest type, Digest)
5. Add DS record at registrar

### Cloudflare:
1. Dashboard → Domain → DNS → Settings
2. Enable DNSSEC
3. Copy DS record details
4. Add DS record at registrar

### Google Cloud DNS:
1. Console → Network services → Cloud DNS
2. Select zone → DNSSEC
3. Enable DNSSEC
4. Copy DS record
5. Add at registrar

### Generic:
1. Enable DNSSEC at DNS provider
2. Get DS record (4 values: Key tag, Algorithm, Digest type, Digest)
3. Log in to domain registrar (GoDaddy, Namecheap, etc.)
4. Add DS record in DNSSEC settings
5. Wait 24-48 hours for propagation
6. Verify: dig +dnssec example.com

registrar.config:
# Domain Registrar Configuration
# For DNSSEC DS Record Addition

## Popular Registrars:

### GoDaddy:
1. Log in to GoDaddy account
2. My Products → Domains
3. Click domain → Manage DNS
4. Advanced Features → DS Records
5. Add DS Record:
   - Key Tag: (from DNS provider)
   - Algorithm: (from DNS provider)
   - Digest Type: (from DNS provider)
   - Digest: (from DNS provider)

### Namecheap:
1. Log in to Namecheap
2. Domain List → Manage
3. Advanced DNS → DNSSEC
4. Add DS Record
5. Enter values from DNS provider

### Google Domains:
1. Log in to domains.google.com
2. Select domain → DNS
3. DNSSEC → Configure
4. Add DS record

### Cloudflare Registrar:
1. Log in to Cloudflare
2. Domain Registration → Manage
3. DNSSEC automatically configured

## DS Record Format:
Key Tag: 12345
Algorithm: 8 (RSA/SHA-256) or 13 (ECDSA P-256/SHA-256)
Digest Type: 2 (SHA-256) or 4 (SHA-384)
Digest: [long hex string]

## Verification:
- Changes take 24-48 hours to propagate
- Check parent zone: dig +short DS example.com
- Verify DNSSEC chain: delv example.com
registrar.reload:
# Registrar changes propagate automatically
# Typical propagation: 1-48 hours

# Check DS record at parent:
dig +short DS example.com

# Verify DNSSEC chain:
delv example.com @8.8.8.8

# If DNSSEC fails after 48 hours:
# 1. Verify DS record matches DNS provider
# 2. Check Key Tag, Algorithm, Digest Type
# 3. Verify Digest value exactly
# 4. Contact registrar support if issues persist
registrar.verify:
# Verify DS Record at Registrar

# Check DS record published:
dig +short DS example.com

# Check from multiple DNS servers:
dig DS example.com @8.8.8.8
dig DS example.com @1.1.1.1
dig DS example.com @208.67.222.222

# Verify DNSSEC validation:
dig +dnssec example.com @8.8.8.8 | grep "ad"
# Should see: flags: qr rd ra ad

# Online DNSSEC validator:
curl https://dnssec-analyzer.verisignlabs.com/example.com

# Expected result: "All OK"
# If errors, review DS record values

OPS_INFRASTRUCTURE.rollbackPlan:
1. Document current DNS records before changes (dig output)
2. Set low TTL (300s) before major changes
3. Test in staging/dev domain first if possible
4. If email delivery breaks after SPF/DKIM/DMARC:
   - Check DMARC reports for failure patterns
   - Temporarily set DMARC p=none (monitor only)
   - Review SPF includes - ensure all mail servers listed
   - Verify DKIM selector and key match mail server config
5. If DNSSEC breaks (site unreachable):
   - Remove DS record at registrar immediately
   - Disable DNSSEC at DNS provider
   - Wait 1-2 hours for cache expiration
   - Verify resolution restored
   - Re-enable carefully with correct DS record
6. If CAA blocks legitimate certificate:
   - Add CA to CAA record immediately
   - CAA changes propagate in 5-15 minutes
   - Retry certificate issuance
7. Keep backup of all DNS records: dig example.com ANY > dns-backup.txt
8. Monitor email delivery metrics for 48 hours post-change
9. Set up alerts for DMARC failures, DNSSEC failures

6. Send test email to check-auth@verifier.port25.com

#!/bin/bash
# Automated DNS Security Test Script

DOMAIN="example.com"
EMAIL_SELECTOR="default"  # Change to your DKIM selector

echo "================================="
echo "DNS Security Test: $DOMAIN"
echo "================================="

# Test SPF
echo -e "\n[1/5] Testing SPF..."
SPF=$(dig +short TXT $DOMAIN | grep "v=spf1")
if [ -n "$SPF" ]; then
    echo "✅ SPF Record Found:"
    echo "   $SPF"
else
    echo "❌ SPF Record Missing"
fi

# Test DMARC
echo -e "\n[2/5] Testing DMARC..."
DMARC=$(dig +short TXT _dmarc.$DOMAIN)
if [ -n "$DMARC" ]; then
    echo "✅ DMARC Record Found:"
    echo "   $DMARC"
    
    # Check policy
    if echo "$DMARC" | grep -q "p=reject"; then
        echo "   ✅ Policy: reject (optimal)"
    elif echo "$DMARC" | grep -q "p=quarantine"; then
        echo "   ⚠️  Policy: quarantine (good, consider reject)"
    elif echo "$DMARC" | grep -q "p=none"; then
        echo "   ⚠️  Policy: none (monitoring only, upgrade to quarantine/reject)"
    fi
else
    echo "❌ DMARC Record Missing"
fi

# Test DKIM
echo -e "\n[3/5] Testing DKIM..."
DKIM=$(dig +short TXT ${EMAIL_SELECTOR}._domainkey.$DOMAIN)
if [ -n "$DKIM" ]; then
    echo "✅ DKIM Record Found:"
    echo "   ${DKIM:0:60}..." # Show first 60 chars
else
    echo "❌ DKIM Record Missing (using selector: $EMAIL_SELECTOR)"
    echo "   Try different selectors: google, default, s1, s2"
fi

# Test CAA
echo -e "\n[4/5] Testing CAA..."
CAA=$(dig +short CAA $DOMAIN)
if [ -n "$CAA" ]; then
    echo "✅ CAA Records Found:"
    echo "$CAA" | while read line; do
        echo "   $line"
    done
else
    echo "⚠️  CAA Records Missing (recommended)"
fi

# Test DNSSEC
echo -e "\n[5/5] Testing DNSSEC..."
DNSSEC=$(dig +dnssec $DOMAIN | grep "flags:" | grep "ad")
if [ -n "$DNSSEC" ]; then
    echo "✅ DNSSEC Validated (ad flag present)"
else
    echo "⚠️  DNSSEC Not Validated"
fi

echo -e "\n================================="
echo "Test Complete"
echo "================================="

# Additional online checks
echo -e "\nRecommended online checks:"
echo "  SPF:    https://mxtoolbox.com/spf.aspx"
echo "  DMARC:  https://mxtoolbox.com/dmarc.aspx"
echo "  DKIM:   Send test email to check-auth@verifier.port25.com"
echo "  CAA:    https://caatest.co.uk/$DOMAIN"
echo "  DNSSEC: https://dnssec-analyzer.verisignlabs.com/$DOMAIN"
